question: What specifically makes narrative prose hard to annotate, compared with the one-line glosses that worked?
why_this_is_safe_to_run_now: It measures properties of the TEXT, not performance against the answers. No correct-answer label is read at any point. So it is not the forbidden move — tuning a reader against a benchmark whose answers I know — and its conclusions cannot be steered by a score.
why_it_is_worth_running: EXP-042 established that a rule-based reader fails on prose, but not WHY. 'Prose is harder' is not actionable. If the gap is one or two specific properties, that tells us what any Stage 2 reader must handle and gives a way to predict failure before spending a commission on it.

data.easy_set: the 60 corpus glosses (mechanical reader: 1.52 relations each, 7 empty)
data.hard_set: the 90 ARN passages (mechanical reader: near-total failure, 69% empty)

measures: explicit causal verbs per passage, using the reader's own declared lexicon
proportion of sentences containing NO lexicon verb
pronoun density, as a proxy for how much reference must be resolved across sentences
named entities and proper nouns, as a proxy for surface specificity that must be abstracted away
statistic: per-measure comparison between the two sets, reported as means with the ratio between them. Descriptive.
tests: two-sided Welch t-test per measure, with Holm correction across the six measures because six comparisons on the same data is six chances to find something.
exclusion_rule: none; every passage in both sets is measured.
robustness: report the measure that separates the sets MOST and check it is not simply length in disguise, by re-running the comparison on a length-matched subset.
falsification: no measure separates the sets after correction -> the difficulty is not captured by any of these surface properties and this diagnostic has failed
only length separates them -> the answer is trivial and unhelpful: prose is longer
the separating measures survive length-matching -> genuinely informative about what a reader must do

predictions.claim: explicit causal verbs per WORD will be far lower in the ARN passages
predictions.reason: the glosses were written to describe causal structure; the narratives were written to tell a story, and stories imply causation through sequence rather than stating it

predictions.claim: pronoun density will be much higher in ARN
the proportion of sentences with no causal verb at all will be the single biggest separator
length alone will NOT explain it -- the separation will survive length-matching
